articleTitle: Decentralized control of multi-area multi-machine overlapping interconnected power systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A decentralized control methodology for automatic generation control (AGC) of multi-area multi-machine overlapping interconnected power systems is proposed in this paper, based on the restriction and aggregation algorithm of the Inclusion Principle. The state space model for the multi-area interconnected power system is decomposed as a group of pair-wise area and/or subsystem models. The decentralized controllers designed by the LQG / H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> control schemes are placed at each pair areas and/or subsystems acted effectively in improving frequency and tie-line power bias stabilization. The effect of the subsystem interconnection described by the tie-line power on decentralized controls is exhibited in each pair subsystems. The application of the decentralized controllers to the system is presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Robust Multiobjective Linear Quadratic State Feedback Control
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper is concerned with the robust state feedback control for uncertain linear systems with multiple quadratic performance objectives. A scalar criterion optimization problem is addressed. Based on the parameter-dependent Lyapunov function approach, iterative LMI algorithms are developed, which are illustrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: State space modelling of distortion compensation in a realistic power network
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Abstract A power system, constituting generators, a distribution system and non-linear consumer loads with hybrid power compensators, is a complex system characterised by changing line impedances and load and generator conditions. The use of sophisticated control techniques in these systems is becoming very important, necessitating the need for accurate system modelling, that is software compatible with controller design programs.

articleTitle: Determination of ADSL data rates over subscriber lines using practical DMT modulation simulation
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line (ADSL) is a high speed access technology which can be used for asymmetric multimedia and Internet applications. A common problem facing telecommunication service providers (Telcos) is to determine beforehand how many customers could be upgraded from existing plain analog voice services, or any other service, to ADSL(+voice) over the same local loop. In this paper the ADSL downstream throughput rate for a specified part of a network, which includes additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN), near-end crosstalk (NEXT) and far-end crosstalk (FEXT) between adjacent lines, is determined. Services being considered are: ADSL, ISDN and El. A bit loading algorithm [1], as used in practical Discrete Multi-Tone (DMT) ADSL modems, is used to determine ADSL downstream data rates.

articleTitle: Detectability of Solutions to Control Systems Through Informations Gathered Along Time
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Given a control problem, informations (e.g., measurements) of the state gathered along time are described by a informational tube. The detector associates with any current time the (possibly empty) subset of states that can be reached by a evolution from the initial time up to the current time “detectable” in the sense it satisfies the given measurements. Once defined, this detector is characterized and studied with the tools of viability theory. In particular, the time derivative of the detector provides the regulation map governing the evolution of the detectable solutions.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of periodic sampled-data H2 and mixed H2 / H∞ control
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper uses a time domain approach for the analysis of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> performance of periodically time varying sampled-data controllers for the rejection of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> disturbances. For the purpose of the analysis, linear time invariant (LTI) controllers are distinguished from linear periodically time varying (LPTV) controllers. For control of an LTI plant, it is shown that the time varying dynamics of the LPTV controller deteriorates the closed loop system H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> performance and an LTI controller can be found to provide strictly better H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> control of the system. For H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> control, it is shown that if a given LPTV controller meets an H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>, constraint, the LTI controller will also meet the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> constraint while giving superior H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> performance.

articleTitle: A network model to optimise cost in underground mine design
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper examines the problem of designing an underground mine so as to optimise the development and haulage costs. It focusses particularly on the costs associated with the ramps and shafts which provide passage to and from the ore zones. This mine optimisation problem is modelled as a weighted network. The controls (variables for the optimisation process) and operational constraints are described. A main constraint in mining networks is that all ramps have gradients no more than a given maximum value m. In this paper we describe the mine design problem as an optimisation problem, and prove that under reasonable conditions the cost function of an underground mining network with maximum gradient constraint m is convex. The convexity of the objective function ensures the existence of minimum cost mining networks, and theoretically any descent algorithms for finding minimal points can be applied to the design of minimum cost mining networks.

articleTitle: A model for the fraction of time availability of the effective earth radius factor for communications planning in South Africa: Part I - The basic model
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper a basic mode! for the cumulative probability distribution of the k-factor, commonly used in radio propagation studies for communications, is proposed. Available South African and Namibian data is used to test the model. Further investigation using regression analysis results in a set of coefficients, which could be used to predict the cumulative probability for various values of the k-factor in South Africa. It is clear from the analyses that there may be climatic factors, which must still be incorporated in the proposed model in a statistical manner. Although the available data is limited in terms of the numbers of observational sites, the proposed model suggests that it may be possible to make significantly better predictions of the k-factor than the simplistic 4/3rds earth approach, and thus to extend the limited coverage of the available observations

articleTitle: A simple hidden markov model for a CDMA channel with correlated rayleigh fading
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper, a simple hidden Markov model (HMM) is derived as an aid to characterising the performance of slotted medium access control (MAC) code division multiple access (CDMA) protocols over correlated multipath Rayleigh fading channels. The HMM is based on a simple two-state (fade, non-fade) channel scheme used in conjunction with a simple threshold model to map the channel state onto the user's observed slot (packet) error process. The parameters of the HMM are obtained both from simulation results and from a theoretical analysis based on functions of the correlation properties of the Rayleigh channel. The HMM is tested for a simple slotted direct sequence CDMA (DS-CDMA) ALOHA protocol, where results show that, despite it's simplicity, the proposed HMM is fairly accurate in modelling packet error sequences.

articleTitle: The upward streamer mechanism versus step potentials as a cause of injuries from close lightning discharges
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A close lightning flash occurred during a soccer match being played in a Johannesburg stadium injuring several players, some seriously. The match was being televised from two directions and the resulting videos show dramatically how various players were affected immediately following the instant of the flash. At least nine players were seen to clasp their heads, and some of those subsequently complained of cramp like pains in their legs, and this is taken as evidence that electric currents flowed from head to foot through them. Of these particular nine players, at least four were filmed with only one foot touching ground, and thus the classical step potential mechanism could not account for their injuries. Thus substantial evidence is presented that the players were more likely to have been subjected to upward directed electric streamers, which, although not detected by the cameras, emanated from the top of their heads and carrying sufficient current to cause the observed physical effects, and in some cases, serious injuries.

articleTitle: Intelligent adaptive control of an industrial fish cutting machine
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper addresses the application of intelligent adaptive control in an industrial process. Implementation of the technique in a practical system should lead to gaining confidence and acceptance of the methodology. An important rationale for the work is the potential of an intelligent adaptive control technique to overcome some shortcomings of conventional control approaches. An intelligent adaptive control (IAC) technique, which is analogous to conventional model-referenced adaptive control (MRAC) is presented. This scheme uses a fuzzy knowledge base and an inference mechanism for making tuning decisions of a lead compensator in the control loop. As a case study, IAC is implemented on an industrial fish processing machine. In order to show the effectiveness of the intelligent scheme, a conventional MRAC is implemented on the same machine, and the performance under the two techniques is compared. It is found that IAC is able to perform as well as MRAC, while possessing better flexibility in design, ease of implementation, and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: An Engineering Introduction to Nonlinear Control
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Control system design has reached a level of considerable maturity and there exists substantial understanding of “standard” linear control problems. The aim of this paper is to look beyond linear solutions and give a brief introduction to Nonlinear Control. We adopt a practical viewpoint so as to introduce this field to those who may not be familiar with it.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The field of automatic control studies the tools required to design systems that maintain desirable performance by sensing and automatically adapting to changes in the environment. Given the rapid advances in information and communication technologies, and the increased availability of sensors, the application of control principles is becoming increasingly frequent and widespread.
